newsitem.title: UAE: Airport must be conduit, less of cargo storage area.
newsitem.headline: Airport must be conduit, less of cargo storage area.

text.p: Airports have to rethink their role in air cargo to become less of a storage area and more of a conduit for freight, the managing director of Unisys' freight programme said on Monday.
"Airports will need to redefine their role in air freight, from full stops to commas," Hugh Doyle said at a cargo conference in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.
"The overall philosophy for all parties along the cycle must be: 'only do work which adds value as perceived by the shipper'," he said.
Doyle said airports of the future should have a minimum of intervention.
"Airports must see themselves as conduits," he said at the two-day conference, which began on Sunday.
Doyle said that 50 percent of freight was in the shed of the airport's arrivals terminal for more than three days, and 27 percent was in the shed for more than five days.
"This is incompatible with the whole concept of air freight which is based on time," he said.

The cargo conference is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a world organisation for airports. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
